title: Matter of Light
note: Every asset here was generated inside the festival project and is public under the festival's rules. They are examples, not templates: look for the thing named under each one, then make your own.

story.label: S22 · the turn
story.why: The last held close-up belongs to whoever changes. The ending was rewritten on Sep 14 to make it Alder's, and this take carries it.

story.label: F35 · the most important single image
story.why: Alder at the end of the push, one dark cloud out of focus behind him. Written and anchored before a second of video existed.

story.label: F01 · almost nothing
story.why: The first frame of the film. Everything the opening does, it does by revealing.

cast.label: Two of the four Souls
cast.why: One identity, trained once. Every state sheet — damaged, ascended, mortal — is generated from it, never re-described.

cast.label: The brothers
cast.why: Same height, age only in the face. Two-person shots cannot use a Soul at all — they run on the elements.

cast.label: A location, three ways on one sheet
cast.why: Intact in daylight, under cannon fire, and from behind looking out to sea. One id, three uses, no drift between them.

cast.label: Two of the four lighting plates
cast.why: Every frame on a board inherits its plate's key. One board per plate is what stops the light drifting.

cast.label: The identity break the model can't see
cast.why: All four takes of S5 attached the mortal sheet while every other shot used the ascended one. Scores rank takes; only a continuity read catches the wrong face.

cast.label: Replaced by hand — and the repo didn't know
cast.why: This element replaced prop_enemy_ships in the web app. Four prompts pointed at the dead id for days. Record old → new the moment you swap.

anchors.label: A shared frame
anchors.why: F02 ends S1 and starts S2. One image doing two jobs, generated once; the seam lives inside the glare.

anchors.label: The match pair
anchors.why: The tear's blue facet becomes open water. Designed as a pair, not found in the edit — made independently, the 108-year jump costs the audience a beat.

anchors.label: B01 · a bridge
anchors.why: The leviathan's flank filling frame to near-black. It has to go genuinely black — 70% obscured reads as a hidden cut that failed.

anchors.label: F17 · scale in one frame
anchors.why: Oriane tiny between the opening jaws. This frame has to carry the shot's whole point alone, because the shot will not cut.

b.label: F23 · its residue on the beach

timing.label: One object carries the cut across a day and three thousand miles
timing.why: The structural hinge between movements. Deciding where this lands is a Gate C decision — after it, moving it costs video.

timing.label: S15 · the zero-generation fix
timing.why: The first five seconds of this take were moved before the vortex so the audience meets the brothers before Oriane dies. The rest stayed. One blade cut, no render.

motion.label: S21 · chained, 16s
motion.why: Chained on F32→F33. Only 2 of 16 renders in the account used start/end frames — both the longest shots, which is exactly right. Chain anything over 12s.

motion.label: Same shot, two creature sheets
motion.why: The left take attaches the film's leviathan; the right attached a different creature entirely. Both scored fine. Read the references, not just the numbers.

motion.label: S1 · one 30s crane
motion.why: It carries S1 and S2 in a single move, exactly as the bible asked. If it has to lose time, it comes off the front — every take here paid on its last second.

sound.label: The opening narration
sound.why: Measured, vast, already grieving. Lay it under the black so the first three seconds are not silent; the crane rises under the voice.

sound.label: “There's something more.”
sound.why: The smile arriving — hope, relief, something braver than either. Four words carry the ending.

sound.label: “Tomorrow.”
sound.why: One word, and it ends the scene. Generate the voice first; attach it as an audio reference; turn the model's own audio off on that shot.

a.label: S1 · the board's pick · current courtyard element
a.why: Chosen for continuity with the S23 bookend.

b.label: S1 · the cut's ♥ · retired courtyard element

cut.label: Element continuity is invisible at a wide — S1
cut.why: The board argued element; the editor argued motion. At 21:9 the two courtyards are one place. Rank continuity arguments by whether a viewer can see them at the shot's size.

cut.label: Selection is the grade
cut.why: Same shot, same boys, one look decision, ten points. A colour pass across two lighting worlds in an hour drifts; picking the graded take does not.

cut.label: S6 · already opens on the match cut
cut.why: It carries the tear-to-ocean cut and the card — which made a planned transition shot redundant. Check what you have before you generate what you planned.

cut.label: F37 · the last frame
cut.why: The frozen tear as one point of light on a vast floor. It rhymes with F01; the end-card plate continues it to black, and the credits go on after, in the NLE.

learn.label: The delivered master · Sep 16
learn.why: The MOV cut after the Sep 15 generations, uploaded into the project root. Stage 8 starts here: upload the master, run the scene analysis, read the favourites against the picks.
learn.from: upload 7b801917 · in the project root 2026-09-16 21:52 UTC

a.label: S20 · the board's pick · scored 52
a.why: The rescoring moved the board to this take.

b.label: S20 · the cut's ♥ · scored 51
b.why: The editor kept the first-read take; one point behind, which is noise.

learn.label: The board's pick lost to the editor's eye — S20
learn.why: The cut favourited the alternate. The board had moved to the scored take; the timeline never did. Show alternates at the pick's size: a board is a proposal.

a.label: S11 · the board's pick · 8s
a.why: One take, wrong sheet, too short.

b.label: S11 · regenerated on the battle sheet · 15s · 46
b.why: Made at 23:04 on deadline night; favourited. Its own audio says 'Thank you' in the last second.

learn.label: Fixed by regenerating, not by choosing — S11
learn.why: When a shot has one take and it is wrong, the fix is a regeneration on the right sheet, not a different pick. Keep that prompt ready before the deadline — and regenerate silent shots with audio off: two of the four deadline-night regenerations came back with the model's own voice in them.

learn.label: NEW-3 · the transition the board called redundant
learn.why: Generated the next day from the S4 take as a video reference, and favourited. Never call a transition redundant on the board; show both and let the timeline decide.

a.label: NEW-1 · the mind divides · 16s · Sep 15
a.why: Written on the board on Sep 14, shot on Sep 15, text-only.

b.label: NEW-2 · the mound · 16s · Sep 15
b.why: Change 3's one generation, made exactly as written.

learn.label: Shot the day after — the board's prompts, verbatim
learn.why: Six generations from the board's own prompts, made after the deadline. Neither favourited. Whether they are in the delivered cut is what the scene analysis answers; the record only says they exist.
